title: Standards Gap Propagation: Quantifying How Absent Standards Cause Downstream Safety Practice Variation

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: empirically demonstrating that standards reduce safety practice variance directly supports mandatory standard-setting as a governance intervention.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Advanced: measuring variance in safety practices across companies and domains requires substantial data collection methodology and statistical analysis beyond beginners.

narrow_scope.reasoning: No clear milestone: cross-domain survey of safety practice variation across multiple companies is a broad data collection challenge with unclear boundaries.

novelty.reasoning: Partially addressed: cross-company safety practice variation is documented by FLI, but the causal role of absent standards in driving that variation has not been isolated.

novelty_assessment.label: partially_addressed
novelty_assessment.reasoning: The FLI AI Safety Index (2024, Winter 2025, Summer 2025) provides cross-company safety practice assessments across 33 indicators and 6 domains, revealing substantial variation (grades range from C+ to F). The finding that 'the gap between firms is widening' and that capabilities accelerate faster than safety practices is documented. The necessity of AI audit standards boards was argued in a 2025 Springer paper. However, the specific causal claim that absent standards cause downstream practice variation (rather than merely correlate with it) has not been rigorously tested. The FLI Index measures variation but does not decompose it by standards presence/absence. The causal propagation mechanism is partially novel.
key_references: FLI AI Safety Index Summer 2025. Future of Life Institute.
FLI AI Safety Index 2024 Full Report. Dec 2024.
The necessity of AI audit standards boards. AI & Society, Springer, 2025.
